newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Feb 5.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Food, gasoline and other products, bought tax-free in Ivory Coast's commercial capital for export to neighbouring countries such as Mali, Burkina Faso and Ghana, is being sold fraudulently before leaving the country, government newspaper investigation shows

- President of the African Development Bank Omar Kabbaj says Bank will hold meeting in Abidjan next week to discuss a capital increase, but says the increase is less pressing than in the past thanks to new credit policy

- Public holiday in Ivory Coast on Thursday for Moslem Night of Destiny feast ahead of the end of the fasting month of Ramadan - Polish trade mission visits Ivory Coast from February 8 to 12 (published announcement)
- Leader of student federation FESCI, Guillaume Soro, arrested; university crisis intensifies
- Two journalists from opposition daily La Voie rough-handled by police after trying to question Soro after his arrest
- Ivorian human rights league LIDHO says in statement that FESCI is a lawful organisation and that government has no right to persecute its militants
- U.S. embassy seeks land or property to turn into a sports and recreation centre and club (published announcement)

- France Telecom sends 15 French expatriates to help develop Ivory Coast's privatised telephone company CI-TELCOM in which it has just bought a 51 percent stake through its France Cables and Radio subsidiary.

- Rally of the Republicans (RDR) and Ivorian Popular Front (FPI), allies within the Republic Front opposition alliance, negotiate separately with the government on constitution of broad-based government

- Ivory Coast sells its shares in tin can-producing company Societe Ivoirienne d'Emballages Metalliques (SIEM), a subsidiary of CARNAUDMETALBOX, as part of its privatisation programme. Price 29,500 CFA francs. Offer of shares closes February 28. (Privatisation Committee advertisement)
- Ivorian coconut processing company SICOR put backs its annual general meeting to Friday February 7 because of public holiday on Thursday
